title: Peer benchmark
reader_question: Where does the borrower sit against comparable peers, and what is the credit implication?

inputs.why: the classified readable issuer and market source inventory
canonical borrower financials, entity, periods and definitions
host-computed borrower credit metrics, with their limitations
supplied peer selection, financial and valuation evidence only
the borrower identity and comparison date

process: Role and pack-source gate. Peer normalization and borrower-versus-peer credit analysis, not an equity valuation. Search the whole supplied issuer/market pack (notes, exhibits and attachments included), name the files searched, and anchor CP-1's entity, run, periods and definitions. Use CP-1 borrower figures unchanged with copied citations; use delivered MODEL figures with calc: MODEL citations, never recompute them. Read a delivered optional MODEL; an absent or Blocked input remains a named limitation. No web discovery or fetching: select from user-provided peers first, then document-disclosed, internal, public-company, transaction and broader-sector candidates already in the pack. A supplied web-origin source retains Web-Scraped — Unverified; it never becomes analyst-selected by relabelling. Record provenance composition and confidence impact.

Peer-First Gate. Complete cp1c.peer_set selection and metric alignment before benchmarking or aggregation. For every candidate record selection source, category (Borrower/Issuer, Direct Operating Peer, Sector Peer, Rating/Leverage Peer, Public Trading Comp, Transaction Comp, Internal RV Peer, Excluded/Not Comparable), strengths, limitations, evidence tier, availability, usability and exclusion reasons within selection_basis/data_availability. Assess all 16 dimensions in comparability rationale: product/service similarity; revenue model; end-market exposure; geography; customer type/concentration; contract structure; margin structure; capex intensity; working-capital dynamics; leverage/capital structure; public vs private; accounting standard; fiscal-period alignment; data availability; valuation relevance; source provenance. A name alone is not financial evidence. Exclude the borrower from its peer distribution.

Apply all 13 exclusion triggers before statistics: no overlapping periods; irreconcilable accounting; different business model; data >18 months stale; insufficient data; distress distortion; irreconcilable perimeter; irreconcilable currency/unit; misleading to committee; web-origin unverifiable; sector overlap unconfirmed; contradicted data; financials behind paywall. Keep excluded candidates and named reasons visible, even though they never enter N. House comparability Close = Comparable; Partial = Comparable with Limitations; Weak = Not Comparable. Insufficient Information stays explicit in the rationale and calculator status; use Weak for the unqualified candidate, never Close by default.

Alignment before statistics. For each peer/metric record in definition_note and Analysis the 11 checks: metric definition; adjustment basis; reporting period; period length; accounting standard; currency; unit; perimeter; data source quality; calculation status; source provenance parity. Also retain AP1 borrower definition, AP2 peer definition, AP3 source period, AP4 currency, AP5 IFRS/US GAAP, AP6 actual/pro forma, AP7 reported/adjusted, AP8 LTM/YTD/quarterly/annualized, AP9 source quality, AP10 normalization, AP11 resulting comparability. Unbridged EBITDA, FYE, lease/pension/intangible, currency, leverage-definition, perimeter or capex mismatches, >12-month period lag, or insufficient source data require Partial/Weak with a reason. Reconcile cited differences explicitly or gate the dependent comparison; no silent currency conversion, period interpolation or normalization.

Benchmarks in cp1c.peer_metrics: one figure per peer/metric, with explicit period, unit_label, currency for absolute amounts, definition and citation. Cover supported operating growth/margins, cash-flow conversion/capex/working capital and leverage/coverage/liquidity. Definition inheritance retains CP-1's gross/net/senior debt, reported/adjusted earnings and cash/P&L interest distinctions. Borrower ratios come from CP-1/MODEL; do not build unsupported CP-1 or Model metrics. Peer calculations state formula, components and lineage; missing component means null, never zero. Record calculation_status (Reported, Calculated, Derived, Provisional, Not Comparable, Insufficient Information), outlier decision and source age in definition_note and typed inputs. No Image-Read value enters arithmetic. Inherit the 15 CP-1 formula definitions without recalculating borrower figures: gross profit/revenue; EBITDA/revenue; EBIT/revenue; net income/revenue; (current-prior revenue)/prior revenue; (current-prior EBITDA)/prior EBITDA; total debt/EBITDA; net debt/EBITDA; senior secured debt/EBITDA; EBITDA/cash interest; (EBITDA-capex)/cash interest; FFO/total debt; FCF/EBITDA; capex/revenue; cash + undrawn committed facilities. Denominator gaps or nonpositive ratio bases remain explicit limitations.

Deterministic statistics. For each metric write typed calculator input to calc/CP-1C-peer_statistics.json (one object per invocation; create calc/ if absent). Preserve additional metric inputs and results only under the module-scoped calc/CP-1C/ directory, creating it if absent; use distinct metric filenames and retain every input/result pair there. Run python <RBOT>/scripts/rbot.py calc peer_statistics --in <RUN>/calc/CP-1C-peer_statistics.json --out <RUN>/calc/CP-1C-peer_statistics.out.json. Required top keys: metric_id, unit_label, borrower_value, peers. Each peer requires peer, value, comparability, calculation_status, period, currency; add unit_label, definition_note, cite, selection_basis, limitation_note, outlier (boolean), outlier_reason, age_months where supported. Top period, currency, definition_note and cite bind the borrower comparison; omit unknown metadata with a visible limitation, never invented text asserting alignment. Figures are decimal strings or integers; missing values are JSON null, not floats or zero. Do not add undeclared keys. Typed sidecars are model-authored inputs, not source evidence.

Copy calculator positioning into cp1c.positioning exactly; add only Module-owned credit_implication and source/calculator citations. The calculator owns min/max/range at N>=2, median at N>=3, quartiles at N>=4, average at N>=5, inclusive R type 7 / Decimal38, delta and Above/In line/Below (exact equality In line). Exclude unqualified, Provisional, null and >18-month data before N. Show N, suppressed-statistic reasons, >12-month staleness, definition/provenance cautions and both including/excluding-outlier versions in Analysis. The canonical row uses the including-qualified-outliers distribution; show the exclusion sensitivity separately in Analysis, never overwrite or duplicate the metric row. Do not rank an incomplete or materially misaligned set. Critical Q1/Q3 or positioning unavailable => — and Blocked, never weakened gates or invented quartiles. A diagnostic calculator median is not permission to claim a qualified sector valuation.

Outliers and credit translation. Assess borrower and peers, quantify each deviation from permitted peer range/median/average, and distinguish operational difference, data-quality issue, comparability misalignment and one-off event. Classify Favorable, Unfavorable, Mixed, Non-Comparable or Insufficient Information; a definition/accounting/perimeter-caused outlier is Non-Comparable. Explain changes in outlier status across periods and their credit effects. Translate into operating, cash-flow, leverage/liquidity, refinancing, valuation-context and downstream implications. An outlier flag/reason is your sourced judgment; the calculator makes no judgment. Retain distorted-average warnings with the median and both versions, including N after exclusion.

Valuation context in cp1c.valuation_multiples only where supplied. Keep Trading and Transaction separate; the house Analyst basis labels an explicitly analyst-asserted observation only, never a calculator group or a substitute for either population. EV = equity value + total debt + minority interests + preferred equity - cash/equivalents - liquid available short-term investments; show cited components or the missing component. Public comps state market-cap date, denominator period/definition and perimeter; transactions state date, type, buyer/seller and contemporaneous financial perimeter. Flag stale multiples >12 months. No averaging non-comparable entities or blending populations; meaningful sector multiples require >=3 comparable datapoints. For indicative EV/EBITDA, EV/Revenue, transaction EV/EBITDA and transaction EV/Revenue, run separate metric inputs with unit_label x, multiple_basis Trading or Transaction and positive borrower_metric on the same period/definition/currency. Copy calculator implied_ev low/median/high; retain assumptions/status and both outlier versions. A private borrower without equity value has only bounded implied-EV context. Uncorroborated web multiples stay Provisional — Web-Sourced and excluded. No unsupported definitive valuation, recovery or debt-coverage claim.

Synthesis and readiness. In Analysis connect each supported comparison through cited evidence -> risk mechanic -> creditor implication for competitive position, PD, FCF durability, leverage tolerance, service capacity, liquidity and refinancing. State the strongest supported counter-case, what would make it win and the conviction/monitoring consequence. Trace a dated downside starting condition -> first operational break -> financial transmission -> leverage/liquidity/refinancing consequence -> observable trigger; name missing numbers instead of inventing them. Reconcile every source/period/definition/perimeter disagreement in one place, with both citations and governing reason or a gap. Gaps name affected peer/metric, downstream impact, severity and lifting source; all uncorroborated web evidence is high severity. End with borrower/peer universe, operating/cash-flow/credit findings, outliers, bounded EV context, provenance confidence and CP-2/CP-3/CP-6 readiness. Pass only when the reader question is answered; Restricted for noncritical limitations; Blocked where required critical statistics or borrower comparison cannot be supported. A Blocked Handoff still emits every table/header, — for unavailable critical cells, named gaps and no citation, per canon.
prohibited: No fetching, invented peers/figures, default comparability, fake zero or lowered minimum-N gates.
No unsupported recomputation of CP-1/MODEL, instrument ranking, investment recommendation, recovery conclusion or definitive equity valuation.
